name: Standing hip extension
summary: Holding a wall, take one straight leg back behind you from the hip without leaning forward — the backward banded kick.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, hands on a wall in front, working leg nearest the phone. Keeping the knee straight and the trunk upright, take the leg back 15–25°, squeeze the buttock, return. With a band, loop it around the working ankle and anchor it in front of you.
brief: Stand side-on with the hands on a wall in front. Keeping the knee straight and the trunk upright, take the working leg back, squeeze the buttock, then return.
why: Side-on, the working ankle travels backward past the hip and how far it gets — as a share of the thigh — counts the rep. Leaning forward to fake the range moves the shoulders forward over the same hip, which is the same reading on the trunk, and a knee that bends or a leg that swings the wrong way are both read directly. The lower back arching is not visible from any single angle.

progress.overLabel: Swinging the leg too far back
progress.overTip: Most people only have 10–15° of true hip extension; the rest comes from arching the back.

tempo: Back 2 s, squeeze 1 s, return 2 s.
progression: Band around the ankle anchored in front.
contraindications: Lower back pain on the swing.

faults.label: Leaning forward to go further
faults.tip: The range is small on purpose. Leaning forward moves the work to the lower back.

faults.label: Bending the knee
faults.tip: A bent knee lets the hamstring take the movement instead of the glute, and shortens the swing the camera sees.

faults.label: Swinging the leg forward
faults.tip: This one goes backward only. Swinging forward is a different exercise and the band is pulling the wrong way.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Brace lightly so the movement comes from the hip, not from the spine extending.

guide.stop: Back pain, or pinching at the back of the hip.
guide.cannotSee: The lower back arching, and how hard the band is pulling.

points.t: Straight knee throughout — a bent one is flagged.
Travels backward only, 15–25°; further than that and the back is doing it.
Upright and still; the shoulders moving forward over the hip is leaning, not extending.
Ribs down, lower back quiet — the camera cannot see this one.
Stays put; it is what the coach measures the swing against.
Back 2 s, squeeze 1 s, return 2 s.

calibrationPose: Stand tall, feet together, hands on the wall in front.
